findings: src/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.cpp: the new IsStringPatternFilter only matches generic function names (contains, like, ilike, regexp_matches, suffix/ends_with and their operator aliases) that take a constant pattern. It names no tables, columns, literals or data sizes, and it applies to any LIKE '%x%' or contains-style table filter.

Only the cardinality estimate changes (0.05 instead of 0.2 when there is no equality filter), so plan choice changes but results cannot. The existing rules still apply: an equality-filter estimate wins, the result is clamped to at least 1, and an empty table still gives 0.

Performance risk: when a pattern matches most rows (e.g. LIKE '%a%'), the estimate will be too low and could pick the wrong build side. The author states this risk. Postgres-style estimators make the same trade-off, and maintainers would accept it as a heuristic.
The diff is small and focused, with no duplicated code, test changes or settings changes.
